title: From Gangbangers To Saviors Of Our Nation

sense.text:
“Obey my voice, and I will be your God, and ye shall be my people.” That is what the Lord told us when he brought us out of Egypt: obey his voice and he will be our God, and walk in all the ways he commanded, “that it may be well unto you.” It would be well unto us.

This is the call to the West Coast. We have been lost too long, caught up in all type of foolishness: gangbanging, hatred, incarceration, homelessness. The Lord is upset, and he is starting to shake this place up and wake it up, and a lot of people are going to come back to the Lord like they are supposed to. That is the name of the class: from gangbangers to saviors of our nation.

“But they hearkened not.” Our people are hardheaded. They “walked in the counsels and in the imagination of their evil heart”: that is what our people are doing today, walking in the imagination of their own minds, not following the Lord, not listening to the Bible, not doing what is right in the sight of God so that he could come and redeem us and get us out of here.

They “went backward, and not forward.” Nothing to build their community up, their households up, themselves up; they gave up the fight. As a nation we are going backwards and have not realized it. Not all of us, but the majority of us is more wicked than righteous, and we are not pushing toward the mark.

“I have even sent unto you all my servants the prophets, daily rising up early.” He sends us out to the streets early, crying with the scriptures in the chief places of concourse to wake the people up and bring them back to him. He sends us into dangerous places and dangerous territories, and we go and do the work of the Lord. We are not trying to wake up everybody; we are looking for his chosen, the needle out of the haystack.

“Yet they hearkened not.” We come to their corners and their neighborhoods and they still do not want to listen to the Lord. They “hardened their neck: they did worse than their fathers.” We are worse than our fathers now, worshipping more gods and more deities than our fathers did.

When we say gangbangers, it is not just red and blue. The fraternities, the sororities, the motorcycle gangs, the car clubs: they are all gangs. The police department, the COs, the Department of Corrections: they are gangs too.

“Thou shalt speak all these words unto them.” We go and tell them what the Lord said, “but they will not hearken.” “Thou shalt also call unto them”: we call them daily, through the fire missions, through youth violence programs, community cleanups, libraries, prisons and hospitals, two by two on the street corners, telling them to return and come back to the Father. “But they will not answer thee.”

“This is a nation that obeyeth not the voice of the Lord their God, nor receiveth correction.” They do not want to receive the correction we give them; they do not want to accept the rebuke handed to them. “Truth is perished, and is cut off from their mouth.”

precepts.why:
Truth is perished from their mouth, and Jeremiah 4 shows why: “For my people is foolish, they have not known me.” His people, not everybody in this world, not everybody who so-called loves him: the twelve tribes of the nation of Israel. He is their God and they have not known him.

“They are sottish children”: sottish means stupid, stupefied. They are stupid children, “and they have none understanding.” They do not understand who they are, what happened to them, what is happening to them, what they are supposed to be doing in life, or how they got in this condition.

“They are wise to do evil.” Our people love evil, and love crime, and the other word for crime is sin: fornication, adulteries, robbing, stealing and killing. “But to do good they have no knowledge.” That is why we rise up early and teach them on these street corners, so they will have no excuse in that day, the day they drop dead or the day Christ returns.

It is what the Deacons brought out going over the turbulent 60s: we stood up and fought in the 60s, then in the 70s and 80s we slid right down the hill, the young lion turned old. We have no knowledge how to do good: how to build our communities, work together, stand strong for the Lord, build our families, or teach the young. The older men used to teach the young men and the older women the young girls; now they are hanging with them and competing with each other.

“Brethren, my heart’s desire and prayer to God for Israel is, that they might be saved.” We are all supposed to have that same desire Paul had: that all Israel could be saved.

“They have a zeal of God, but not according to knowledge.” All these gangs, the fraternities, the sororities, the bikers, say they believe in God. They have crosses on their necks, Cesare Borgia on their arms, prayer hands on their arms and on their chains. They think that cross is going to protect them, and that having a Bible in the car is going to help them, without opening it up and reading and applying what it says. God gave us ways out, and they refuse them and run backward, not forward.

“Going about to establish their own righteousness”: you only live once; I got to do what I got to do; I got to feed my kids. They do not think as a community or as a nation; they think as individuals, the way the United States taught us. They “have not submitted themselves unto the righteousness of God”, they have not submitted to this Bible yet. Some of them are going to change. We are going to show who these so-called gangs are according to the Bible, because God is talking about them.

sense.text:
“For man also knoweth not his time.” Man does not know when he is going to drop dead. The Most High gave us time by his Son coming down and giving his life, and every day you wake up is a time to repent, to change, to get your slate clean, to get right with your brother and your sister and walk right in the sight of the Heavenly Father. We woke up this morning to cast off all the wickedness.

“As the fishes that are taken in an evil net”, swooped out of the water, “and as the birds that are caught in the snare”, snatched out of the air: “so are the sons of men snared in an evil time.” We are snared in an evil time right now. It is hard to go in these streets, hard to go to the store: bullets flying, robbery, gangbangers, homelessness, drug dealers, a whole slew of things to pass just to get your food and get back home.

Israel, do not think it is a good time. We are living in the last days and perilous times are at hand; that is what the Bishop and the Deacons have been going over. It comes “when it falleth suddenly upon them”, and they will not know when, whether it is the day you drop dead or the day Christ returns. A small remnant is going to return, so we have to go out in these streets and find them. We are fishermen, fishing for our people right now, before we turn to hunters.

Just in Los Angeles there are over 450 gangs: Bloods, Crips, Sureños, cholos, MS-13 and the rest, Crips fighting Crips and Bloods fighting Bloods, with no structure among them. Chicago has over 90 gangs with over 150,000 members, and America over 33,000 gangs, not counting the crews, the drug dealers, the fraternities and sororities. Many of them never leave their own neighborhood, so we have to go into the Blood neighborhoods, the Crip neighborhoods, the Piru neighborhoods, the MS-13 and Sureño neighborhoods, and teach them this word and wake up the ones God is calling. The Bishop tried to put together a program for ex-gang members to be an example to the men still in it, and we are going back to that program.

“If thou shalt hearken diligently unto the voice of the Lord thy God, to observe and to do all his commandments.” That is all we had to do: listen diligently to the voice of our God and do the things he told us. Then “the Lord thy God will set thee on high above all nations of the earth.” We were supposed to be up high, over all these nations, ruling this earth in righteousness right now.

“If thou wilt not hearken unto the voice of the Lord thy God”, “all these curses shall come upon thee, and overtake thee.” All these curses would come upon us and overtake us if we did not do what he said, and that is what we are living now: the curses of Deuteronomy 28:15 and down. That is the evil net for the fishes and the snare for the birds; that is why men are trapped in the evil time.

“The Lord shall send upon thee cursing, vexation, and rebuke.” Vexation is the state of being annoyed, frustrated or worried: irritation, exasperation, anger, rage. We are mad as hell inside, full of the fury of the Lord, but our people do not know how to vent. We do not know how to let off the steam or which way to direct the anger, so we take it out on each other. The Lord tells us to come back to his book, our record book, and he will teach us to let the steam off in a righteous way.

“Until thou be destroyed, and until thou perish quickly; because of the wickedness of thy doings, whereby thou hast forsaken me.” We call ourselves everything but the children of God, everything but Israelites: Egyptologist, Buddhist, monk, Christian, Roman Catholic. Because we did not listen to our God, he put us in his trick bag: Bloods fighting Bloods, Crips fighting Crips, Bloods fighting Crips, and in the penitentiaries the northern kingdom against the southern kingdom. It is all confusion, a trick bag for us to go at each other.

But God is calling his people back right now. The 350 years from 1619 to 1969 are up, and slowly but surely we are waking up to who we are and trying to get back to our land. America is not our homeland. Judah especially has nowhere to go: everybody else says they are going back to their country, but the bulk of Judah is trapped here in America, fighting our enemy day in and day out and getting killed left and right, because the curses are put upon us.

“The Lord shall smite thee with madness.” We are out of our damn mind. We fight each other over colors, over blocks and territory that do not even belong to us, over something somebody said on the internet, over a stepped-on sneaker or what you looking at. Israel is out of their damn mind.

“And blindness, and astonishment of heart.” When we see each other in the street we just have to shake our heads, we are in such a low condition, never mind the other nations shaking their heads.

“And thou shalt grope at noonday, as the blind gropeth in darkness.” Israelites are groping at noonday: out early in the morning at the liquor store at nine and ten o’clock, at the weed dispensary rolling blunts, because we do not know who we are and feel we cannot function in this society unless we have some type of drug in us. “And thou shalt not prosper in thy ways.” We are showing them how the Bible is going to get them back in order and make us a nation once again.

precepts.why:
This is that astonishment of heart. “All that pass by clap their hands at thee; they hiss and wag their head.” They see us homeless and drug-addicted, leaning all over in Philadelphia, San Francisco, Oakland, Los Angeles, New York, Arizona and Vegas, all doped up, and they hiss and wag their head at us.

“Is this the city that men call The perfection of beauty, The joy of the whole earth?” Are these the people who ruled the earth at one time and created everything to make this earth run? Look at the condition they have them in: drugs, gangs, violence, low jobs, white women destroying us, and the people split into rich, middle class and poor, all in the trick bag. Yet we are still the joy of the whole earth: even in this lowest state, when we sag our pants the world sags its pants, and whatever we say and do, everybody follows.

“All thine enemies have opened their mouth against thee: they hiss and gnash the teeth.” All of them, Edom, Ishmael, Ammon, Moab, Ham and Japheth. “We have swallowed her up”: we destroyed them with the drugs; the athletes get the white women, who have a baby by them and take their money. “Certainly this is the day that we looked for.” They love this time, when we are out here shooting each other over colors and over words on the internet; with vexation on us we make their job that much easier. They pay us on Friday so we party and break the Sabbath from Friday sundown to Saturday sundown, then go to church on Sunday, the wrong day.

“We have found, we have seen it.” “The Lord hath done that which he had devised”: that is Deuteronomy 28, 15 and down. But God has righteous men on this earth who will put their lives on the line to get our people back in order. He put his words in our mouth to build this nation back piece by piece and brick by brick, back to righteousness and glory and an everlasting kingdom nobody is going to destroy.

This shows how the blind grope in darkness. “Their feet run to evil, and they make haste to shed innocent blood.” Our feet run to evil; we are quick to put somebody to death. They are so bold they kick in doors, run into a man’s house while he is taking care of his family, steal cars out of driveways and ravage each other’s houses. That is the vexation in us.

“Their thoughts are thoughts of iniquity”: sin is in our minds all the time. We are wise to tear each other down instead of building each other up. The fraternities and sororities worship other gods, following the Greeks and the old Egyptian gods, and think they are better than their people. “Wasting and destruction are in their paths.”

“The way of peace they know not.” They do not want beef, they want a problem: a way to take their anger out on somebody, beat down their own brother, rob their sister. “There is no judgment in their goings”: nobody telling them this is wrong. We are the ones standing up against the LGBTQ and the ADL and the JDL calling everything anti-Semitic. “They have made them crooked paths: whosoever goeth therein shall not know peace.”

“We wait for light, but behold obscurity; for brightness, but we walk in darkness.” We look for the right path, but we walk in sin; our people love killing, stealing and robbing, not healing, building and creating. “We grope for the wall like the blind, and we grope as if we had no eyes”: we stare each other up and down and hate each other and do not know why, put on a fake smile for the white man and frown at our brother. We have no vision, no foresight. Black and Hispanic people have information that could build our neighborhoods, but we keep it to ourselves just to say I got one over on him.

“We are in desolate places as dead men.” That is why we are caught up in the gangs, the fraternities, the drug dealing and the homelessness: the spirit of the Lord has not woken them up yet. Israel United in Christ is going around the world reviving the people and bringing them back to life. Not all of them will come, but our job is to reach the ones that do, and have things ready for them when they want to change.

sense.text:
“The ox knoweth his owner.” The ox is a big dumb animal, but he knows who owns him. “And the ass his master’s crib”: the donkey knows where he lives; take him miles away and let him go and he will find his way back home. “But Israel doth not know”: the blacks, the Latinos and the Native American Indians do not have a clue. We do not know who owns us or where our homeland is. We are happy here in America at the bottom, the lowest of the lows; they say we are all equal, but we get the short end of the stick because we do not know who owns us or where we are from.

“My people doth not consider.” Israel does not even consider that we are serving slavery because we broke our God’s laws and rules. Our kids and grown men are trapped in the gang life, and a movie about the gangs spread it from California across the whole country; that popular persuasion made our people worse.

“Ah sinful nation, a people laden with iniquity.” Blacks, Latinos and American Indians are one nation, Israel, even though they divided us and conquered us, and God is bringing us back together into that one stick.

A gangbanger on a mission crosses the invisible line into another hood and passes up the man dressed square, passes up a man of a different race, and goes for the one who dresses like him, walks like him and has his body language. He is looking for himself on the other side of town, not his real enemy. That is the vexation of Deuteronomy 28:20: full of anger with no way to vent it, we look for the closest Negro or the closest Latino who looks just like us.

“Hear the word of the Lord, ye children of Israel: for the Lord hath a controversy with the inhabitants of the land, because there is no truth, nor mercy, nor knowledge of God in the land.” “By swearing, and lying, and killing, and stealing, and committing adultery, they break out, and blood toucheth blood.” We are killing, lying, stealing and swearing, blood touching blood. Our people are full of anger and evil against each other; the one hunting on the other side of town is not going after white people or Chinese people, he is hunting down his own people to put them to death. We are not about building our nation up or helping a brother stand up while we stand up; we are about tearing each other down, crabs in the barrel. That is Israel.

precepts.why:
This is a basic commandment our people forgot, even back then. “Thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart.” If you had no hate for your brother, you would not be out trying to find yourself on the other side of town.

“Thou shalt in any wise rebuke thy neighbour, and not suffer sin upon him.” If you had a problem with your brother you would tell him what his issue was, talk it out, and neither of you would carry that sin.

“Thou shalt not avenge, nor bear any grudge against the children of thy people.” If we understood that vengeance against our brother is sin, and that the Lord would put you to death for it, we would not be taking him out for some foolish reason. Because we never learned it, Christ came and said, I give you a new commandment, that you love your brother. It was never new; it was always there, and he had to bring it back to our memory that this is your brother.

A boy is shot on the ground in a drive-by, and the one standing there is asked if he saw anything, and he says no. “And if a soul sin, and hear the voice of swearing, and is a witness, whether he hath seen or known of it; if he do not utter it, then he shall bear his iniquity.” A whole group got shot and he was one of them; he is in iniquity over his brothers.

It is tit for tat against our own people: they kill us, we kill them, back and forth until somebody gives up, and nobody gives up. A seventeen-year-old in 1988 said he is down to die for the Bloods and could not say what the cause is. Our people do not even consider why they do what they do. That is the madness and blindness of Deuteronomy 28 in full effect. If we apply what the Bible tells us to do, we will be a much better people.

sense.text:
“My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge.” The knowledge the Israelites are lacking today is the Bible. There are churches on every corner and nobody is getting the message. “Because thou hast rejected knowledge, I will also reject thee”: our people reject this Bible instead of opening it and seeing ourselves in the record book, seeing that this is us God is talking to and about, so he rejects us, and that is why we are getting shot down in the streets.

“Seeing thou hast forgotten the law of thy God.” They do not care about the laws anymore. We tell the women to put on dresses and the men to marry these sisters, and a lot of them do not want to keep the laws. But God put his word in our mouth to bring his people back from their evil, wicked ways to righteousness.

“As they were increased, so they sinned against me.” As Israel United in Christ grows, many coming in still have their spirits and minds not right, holding on to the world. But we have to keep the sanctuary, a place of refuge, open and ready for them to come and change. Many are called but few are chosen.

“Therefore will I change their glory into shame.” At one time we had Black Wall Street; Durham, North Carolina; the town in Florida where Disney sits; Seneca Village where Central Park is; the black towns they flooded under Lake Martin in Alabama and under a lake in Georgia. We were a great people, but he turned it into shame because we went away from his Bible and stopped teaching the laws to our sons and daughters.

precepts.why:
What is the knowledge they lack? “For the priest’s lips should keep knowledge.” The pastors’ and preachers’ lips should be teaching people to keep God’s laws, so they will not be out there killing and fighting each other for no reason and can understand what they are doing wrong and start doing it right. It is that simple.

“And they should seek the law at his mouth: for he is the messenger of the Lord.” He is supposed to be, but he is not. They tell people the laws are done away with, come as you are, as long as you pay tithes; they are sleeping with people in the church. We are the messengers of the Most High, the prophets back on this earth again, going to the ghettos and the barrios and putting our lives on the line to get God’s word to the people.

sense.text:
“There shall be a confusion also in many places, and the fire shall be oft sent out again, and the wild beasts shall change their places.” A lot of you are going to come out of these fraternities and these gangs and stop selling drugs, because you are going to see it is a dead-end street.

“And menstruous women shall bring forth monsters.” That is what is going on today. These kids are monsters: I kill them, they come back and kill us, and killing is nothing to them. They feed off of blood, crime and sin.

A young gang leader says the gang is his family: we help each other, support each other, rely on each other. Fatherless homes, mothers on welfare for generations, on dope or hustling: that is where the gang becomes the family. And the pastor going out to them is not teaching them how to change; he wants their tithe money, and brings them out of one part of hell into another, with white images of Jesus and the angels.

This is who that pastor is. “For they that are such serve not our Lord Jesus Christ, but their own belly.” He is not really going out to pull these guys off the streets or help them change their lives; he is feeding his own belly, walking them into another part of hell with Cesare Borgia, the white angels and the Sunday lies. Singing and clapping and feeling good does not change your life; he is not giving them the words of the Bible.

“And by good words and fair speeches deceive the hearts of the simple.” He deceives them into worshipping on Sunday, the wrong day, looking at white angels and crosses and idols all over the church. Stained windows: really it is their souls that are stained.

The gang members feel like a family, but that is not family, because they kill each other: Crips fighting Crips and Bloods fighting Bloods. We have to teach our people how to come out of that.

“Woe unto them that call evil good, and good evil.” They call it family and getting money together, but they get money robbing, stealing and killing their own people. “That put darkness for light”: they put Satan for Christ. “And light for darkness”: the right way to walk and live they call darkness.

What we are doing that is good, they call evil: they call us deceivers, liars, fake, Power Rangers, curse us out and give us the middle finger, while they call what they are doing good. They do not know brotherhood. Real brotherhood is when we can rebuke each other, correct each other and hold each other accountable according to the Bible, not according to how we feel.

“Therefore as the fire devoureth the stubble, and the flame consumeth the chaff, so their root shall be as rottenness, and their blossom shall go up as dust”: it is all going to disappear. “Because they have cast away the law of the Lord of hosts”: they do not want to keep the laws in the Bible. That so-called family and brotherhood are demonic brothers, and we have to wake some of them up and bring them back to the Heavenly Father.

They have “despised the word of the Holy One of Israel.” When we teach in the streets they think we came down out of the sky, but we come from the same walks of life and dealt with the same things. The only difference is we found our way back to who we are: the Israelites, with Christ a black man, and everlasting life for those who fight a good fight to the end. Even the churches are a gang: Christianity is a gang and a cult, and Republican and Democrat are gangs. We have to come out of all this foolishness and come back to the Bible.

“For they that are after the flesh do mind the things of the flesh.” That is all they know; they cannot see past this flesh to anything spiritual. That is why they are blind and groping. “But they that are after the Spirit the things of the Spirit.”

“For to be carnally minded is death.” I kill them, they kill us: that carnal mind is death. There is no end to the gangs except three: jail, death, or getting lucky and changing your life and moving away. “But to be spiritually minded is life and peace.”

“The carnal mind is enmity against God: for it is not subject to the law of God, neither indeed can be.” If you are in this flesh you are against the Heavenly Father, against this Bible and the laws, statutes and commandments he gave you.

“So then they that are in the flesh cannot please God.” Walking in this flesh we cannot please God, and flesh and blood cannot enter heaven. We have to be transformed into a different person, changed to righteousness: put off this old tabernacle and put on the righteous one, get the old man off us.

On the news a thirteen-year-old was shot and his father and sister killed because the boy wore the wrong color hat; a woman killed by misidentification. Blood touching blood, and the reporter is the one shaking his head at us, like Lamentations said. The Crips say it is not about money, it is about protecting the homeboys, and that they would die for their homeboy, but a good job still would not stop them cripping. Some of those brothers will come out of that lifestyle; they have the zeal of Romans 10, a zeal not according to knowledge.

“Thou shalt not follow a multitude to do evil.” He says he would die for his homeboy, and that homeboy might stop gangbanging and move somewhere else, and he just gave his life for him. Die for what? For a color? “Neither shalt thou speak in a cause to decline after many to wrest judgment.”

“Thy sons have fainted, they lie at the head of all the streets.” That is what they do: up and down the street corners, in the middle of the block in front of the bodegas in New York, around the strip malls out here. “As a wild bull in a net”: mad as hell, running around killing and shooting each other, attacking each other.

“They are full of the fury of the Lord, the rebuke of thy God.” That goes back to the vexation and the cursing of Deuteronomy 28:15 and down: we broke our God’s laws, and now we are groping, mad, and serving our enemies.
“Thou afflicted, and drunken, but not with wine.” They are drunk off of a philosophy, drunk off of whatever they believe in, drunk off them colors. Why are we killing each other over colors?

“Hope deferred maketh the heart sick.” They are looking for a way out, out of the ghetto to a better life, but they do not know how to get it. They look for brightness and find themselves in darkness. We are the way out for them: this Bible is going to bring them out of the deep dark state they are in and lead them back into righteousness and into the light. “But when the desire cometh, it is a tree of life.”

A Klansman said it plainly: the Klan does not have to kill blacks anymore; just drop off liquor and guns in their town and let them keep killing each other in record numbers. That is what Esau is doing; they find boxes of guns by the train rails in Chicago. That is hope deferred: they have no vision, so the people perish. We have to give them the vision.

A man in the penitentiary said it: you will kill a man over a street you do not own and a color, then come inside and never touch one of those same dudes, because inside the blacks stick together. Our minds are destroyed as a people. And the young men themselves say nobody is rich in the ghetto, and if they could start over they would not turn down that wrong path. One goes to school every day and means to take his friends and family with him out of the ghetto, because nobody told them gangbanging was no good, and someone has to tell the next generation. It comes down to a lack of family: it should never have been the OGs in the neighborhood raising them, but the father teaching his sons.

Some of these men are going to change, get out of that lifestyle and realize who they are and what they are supposed to be doing. There is hope and a way out; you are not stuck there.

“And be not conformed to this world”: not to the gang members, not to the drug dealers, not to sin and an evil, crooked life. “But be ye transformed”: change. You have examples right before you. “By the renewing of your mind”: come back to these scriptures and renew your mind, change your way of thinking, stand up on your feet with the breath of life blown into you, and stop being that dead man.

A lot of these brothers are going to change, because we are out there giving them hope. We tell them to stop killing each other, get a career, stay in school, grow up to be somebody, build their neighborhood and community. You are either part of the destruction or part of the rebuilding.

“Awake to righteousness, and sin not; for some have not the knowledge of God: I speak this to your shame.” They do not have the knowledge of God because nobody is out there teaching them; the young man said nobody told them. So we are going to be a father to the fatherless, give them the knowledge of this Bible and build them back up into great men who become saviors. Because they were in that lifestyle, they can connect with those still in it and be a better example. That is why God is bringing us out of all walks of life, gang members, military, college, professional athletes, and turning them into saviors for his people.

“Thou shalt not commit adultery, Thou shalt not kill, Thou shalt not steal, Thou shalt not bear false witness, Thou shalt not covet.” We are going to teach that to the people and change their minds through the words of the record book. Do not desire what somebody else has; work and get your own.

“Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.” That is what they need in their spirit: not to hate or kill their neighbor, but to love him and build with him while he builds with you. That is how we build a nation.

“Love worketh no ill to his neighbour: therefore love is the fulfilling of the law.”

“Now it is high time to awake out of sleep.” Now is our time, Israel, to stand up and wake up, hit these streets on the fire missions and do the work of the Lord, because our people have been sleeping too long in sin, crime and wickedness. “For now is our salvation nearer than when we believed”: we are closer to the last days.

“The night is far spent, the day is at hand: let us therefore cast off the works of darkness”: put off the old man, the old things we used to do. “And let us put on the armour of light”: put on his Bible, put on Christ, and come back to our righteousness. We have to start becoming those saviors changing the minds and the lives of our people. There is hope, Israel.

“And now, saith the Lord that formed me from the womb to be his servant, to bring Jacob again to him.” He formed them from the womb to be his servant, like he did us. That is why we cannot give up on anybody or write anybody off: we do not know who God has chosen. Our job is to go teach and feed them this truth.

“It is a light thing that thou shouldest be my servant.” To turn somebody from wickedness to righteousness, from darkness to light, is a light thing for him; but we have to go out and do our job, feed them the word of God and teach them there is a way out, that they are not boxed in or cut off.

“To raise up the tribes of Jacob, and to restore the preserved of Israel.” That is our job, Israel: to restore the nation back to greatness, back to the Heavenly Father in the faith of his Son Jesus the Christ. “I will also give thee for a light to the Gentiles, that thou mayest be my salvation unto the end of the earth.”

precepts.why:
Ananias did not trust Saul, because Saul was a demon at the time, ravaging Israel’s houses and putting them to death. “But the Lord said unto him, Go thy way: for he is a chosen vessel unto me.” Saul means destroyer and Paul means builder.

So some of these men in the gangs and in these corrupt lives are chosen vessels, and we have to wake them up through the word of God: plant the seed, water it, and God gives the increase, and they wake up and come out and start doing the work, “to bear my name before the Gentiles”, before the northern kingdom, “and kings, and the children of Israel.” “For I will shew him how great things he must suffer for my name’s sake.”

sense.text: “The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul”: it changes the soul from darkness into light. “The testimony of the Lord is sure”: the word of God is not going to fail. “Making wise the simple”: these brothers are running around with a simple mindset, an incarcerated mindset, a gangbanging, drug dealer, homeless, robbing and stealing mindset, and the law makes them wise.

“The statutes of the Lord are right, rejoicing the heart: the commandment of the Lord is pure, enlightening the eyes.” Once people hear this word they know it makes sense and they can relate to it, and that is what is going to change them. But they have to know the Bible is talking about them: written to them, from them and for them.

precepts.why:
That is why the commandment enlightens the eyes. “That the God of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of glory, may give unto you the spirit of wisdom and revelation in the knowledge of him”: that is the increase he gives, in the knowledge of Christ. “The eyes of your understanding being enlightened.”

“That ye may know what is the hope of his calling.” Hope deferred is for the ones out in the world. In here we have hope: a chance to change, to grow, and to get the kingdom of heaven, if we apply this Bible to our lives, walk right in the sight of God, endure, fight a good fight and go out and do our job waking our people up. This is not like the church where you come in and sit. The Bishop told the class we are not here to be professional students: our job is to go out and teach, to be saviors to our people and enlighten them with the word of God. “And what the riches of the glory of his inheritance in the saints”: in the Israelites.

sense.text:
“Therefore if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature.” If we have repented and converted and changed. A lot of people think because they have friends in red or blue they already made it to the kingdom. No: you have to change, follow and apply, put on his Bible and his armour day in and day out to survive the wiles of the devil.

“Old things are passed away”: your old life is done; put it away and do not go back to it. “Behold, all things are become new”: you get a new start, like Saul got a new start as Paul.

“And all things are of God, who hath reconciled us to himself by Jesus Christ”: he brought us back together. “And hath given to us the ministry of reconciliation.” That is why we have to bring our people back to the Heavenly Father in the faith of Christ: go out and be the saviors to our people and wake them up.

precepts.why:
This is how the old things pass away. “That ye put off concerning the former conversation the old man”: put off that old talk, that wicked, evil, worldly talk, and put on his Bible. The old man “is corrupt according to the deceitful lusts”; the old man is filthy, so your mind has to be changed.

“And be renewed in the spirit of your mind.” “And that ye put on the new man, which after God is created in righteousness and true holiness.” You are not wicked, not evil, not banging, not out here slinging, not carrying that incarcerated mindset anymore. You have become a new man in Christ, and you go out and teach your people.

sense.text: “Gather yourselves together, yea, gather together, O nation not desired.” We Israelites are not desired by the rest of the world, so we have to gather ourselves together under this Bible, under its true holiness, in righteousness and sincerity, not playing games: making a change to our people, our community and our nation. “Before the decree bring forth, before the day pass as the chaff, before the fierce anger of the Lord come upon you, before the day of the Lord’s anger come upon you.”

“Now thanks be unto God, which always causeth us to triumph in Christ.” We are going to triumph in Christ. “And maketh manifest the savour of his knowledge”: we are going to make it plain and bring it out. “By us in every place”: by you brothers who used to live evil, crooked lives and are waking up now and coming back to this truth to serve God in righteousness. You are going to be an example to your community that they can change: a mentor, a big brother, a father to the fatherless, once you get yourself right in this truth.
“For we are unto God a sweet savour of Christ, in them that are saved, and in them that perish.” We go and teach this word so they can be saved in Christ.

“To the one we are the savour of death unto death.” When some people hear the rebuke coming out, we are like death to them. We are marking them, so when Christ comes they have no cloak and no excuse. “And to the other the savour of life unto life”: we breathe the scriptures into them and bring them back to life, like Ezekiel 37, out of the valley of dry bones and standing on their feet. “And who is sufficient for these things?”

“For we are not as many, which corrupt the word of God: but as of sincerity, but as of God, in the sight of God speak we in Christ.” We are going to speak the words of Christ and the truth, and be those saviors who shake this world up, coming out of a low state.

precepts.why: This is the work of making his knowledge manifest in every place. “And the lord said unto the servant, Go out into the highways and hedges, and compel them to come in, that my house may be filled.” We have to go out to the highways and hedges, the corners and the blocks, so his house can be filled.

sense.text: “And they that understand among the people shall instruct many.” These people are going to come up out of that dead estate and start instructing many: to be leaders, to be saviors, to be an example to our people. “Yet they shall fall by the sword, and by flame, by captivity, and by spoil, many days.”

“Now when they shall fall, they shall be holpen with a little help: but many shall cleave to them with flatteries.” Those who understand and instruct many are holpen with a little help, and that little help is shown in the Maccabees: Judas Maccabeus rising up for his people, and his brethren helping him. We need our brothers to come out of that lifestyle and be that little help.

precepts.why:
This is who the little help is. “Then his son Judas, called Maccabeus, rose up in his stead.” Judas Maccabeus stood up and was that little help for his people. “And all his brethren helped him”: that is what we need, our brothers to stand up and help us push this truth, to come out of that lifestyle and live a righteous life and be that little help, a savior to their people. “And they fought with cheerfulness the battle of Israel.”

“So he gat his people great honour, and put on a breastplate as a giant.” That is what the leaders of Israel United in Christ are doing: bringing great honour to Israel in many different ways. “In his acts he was like a lion, and like a lion’s whelp roaring for his prey.”

“For He pursued the wicked, and sought them out, and burnt up those that vexed his people.”
He burnt up them that vexed his people, and Obadiah shows who rises up: “And saviours shall come up on mount Zion to judge the mount of Esau; and the kingdom shall be the Lord’s.”

It says the same thing: “Therefore thou deliveredst them into the hand of their enemies, who vexed them.” “And in the time of their trouble, when they cried unto thee, thou heardest them from heaven.” We cried to God and he heard us from heaven.

“And according to thy manifold mercies thou gavest them saviours, who saved them out of the hand of their enemies.” He gave us saviors: he sent his righteous men, the prophets, back to this earth to get this work done.

“Now hath pride and rebuke gotten strength, and the time of destruction, and the wrath of indignation.” “Now therefore, my sons, be ye zealous for the law.” Zealous is to be full of great energy. “And give your lives for the covenant of your fathers”: become a savior, ready to give your life in this fight, in this truth, for the agreement of our fathers.

“Call to remembrance what acts our fathers did in their time.” We have to call these things to remembrance, Israel. This is no time to get comfortable; it is time to stand up. “So shall ye receive great honour and an everlasting name.”

“And now, brother, behold what glory; and see the people that come from the east: Unto whom I will give for leaders, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, Oseas, Amos, and Micheas, Joel, Abdias, and Jonas, Nahum, and Abacuc, Sophonias, Aggeus, Zachary, and Malachy, which is called also an angel of the Lord.”

Those are the leaders God said he sent: saviors he gives to us. Malachi is called an angel of the Lord, and the angels are the messengers of the Lord. We are the messengers of the Lord, Israel. Be strong in the Lord and in the power of his might.
